messages.subject: Multi-session capthist question
parts:
Dear Jürgen,


I am trying to create a multi-session capthist for my camera-trap study, which will be used in the SECR package for mark-resight analysis. In my study, I have 4 sessions; each with 17, 15, 15 and 15 occasions, respectively. While reading the CamtrapR manual, I did not find the option to take into consideration multiple sessions, other than by adding the argument ‘SessionCol’ in the SpatialDetectionHistory function.


So far, I ran the RecordTableIndividual function and added a column called ‘SessionCol’ in this record table. Based on the date of capture for each record, I attributed the corresponding session number (1, 2, 3 or 4). I ran the SpatialDetectionHistory function using this data, with the SessionCol argument. I realize that the resulting capthist object contains all 62 occasions (of the entire dataset) for each session. In other words, the ‘Usage range by occasion’ and the ‘Counts by occasion’ for each session spans from Occasion 1 to 62 (But for, for example, Session 1 has no detections between occasions 18 and 62).


Also, the resulting SDH table contains occasion IDs ranging between 1-62 rather than 1-17 for Session 1, 1-15 for Session 2, etc. It seems to me that this will cause problems when using the read.capthist function of the SECR package, since the occasion IDs are not separated per session. (If I understand correctly)


I also realised that the occasions were divided by occasion length throughout the entire data period, regardless of the time period for each session. For example, say that the occasion length is specified to 10 days, but Session 1 spans from day 1 to day 98: From what I can see, when using the function spatialdetectionhistory, day 99 and day 100 would be included in the 10th occasion (along with days 91 to 98) and, consequently, the 10th occasion would be split between Session 1 and Session 2.


I was wondering if I missed a step in my approach, or if there was a different way to separate the sessions with CamtrapR (Other than creating a camera operation matrix and SDH for each session separately). I am happy to provide further information, if needed.


Thank you very much in advance,


Vanessa

parts:
You have 2 possibilities to define sessions in spatialDetectionHistory() by adding a sessionCol in: 

1) recordTable (which you chose)
2) camera trap table.

Option 1 is for situations in which cameras were run continuously and you wish to cut that period into sessions. Option 2 is suitable if you used different cameras between sessions or if cameras were moved between sessions. 

Which situation are you in? 

You could try adding a sessionCol in the camera trap table (the equivalent of data(camtraps)). It would require duplicating the entries for the different sessions and adapting the setup/retrieval dates. I don't know if that will solve the issue and haven't tested it yet. 

You could try with a sample data set and also send it to me (or share here) if you wish to. I don't have a multi-session data set to test with at the moment. It would be easier for me to check with a sample data set. 

Best,
Jürgen

Hi Vanessa,
I think it should work now. Please run both attached scripts and then just run spatialDetectionHistory on your native input tables. CTtable needs a session column, recordTable not. 
The function will assign sessions to the records based on the session dates in CTtable. 
Please note that you need to prepare the camera operation table by treating the sessions as cameras (see code below). This is just a workaround and not ideal, but should work as long as you don't have multiple cameras AND multiple sessions per station. 

Based on the code and data you sent me, try the code below. It seems to work for me.

Note the following though:
- the number of stations differes between sessions (station 18 was not set up in session 2 in your data)
- argument "occasionStartTime" should be set to 0 (records may end up in wrong sessions if it is not 0 and records are close to the break between sessions)

- The first occasion of session 2 has only 1 day. The last occasion of session 1 has 5 days (at an occasion length of 6 and with day1 = “survey”). This is because of day1 = "survey"

 

Regarding your other questions:

Also, the resulting SDH table contains occasion IDs ranging between 1-62 rather than 1-17 for Session 1, 1-15 for Session 2, etc. It seems to me that this will cause problems when using the read.capthist function of the SECR package, since the occasion IDs are not separated per session. (If I understand correctly)

Depends on argument day1. If day1 = "survey", it is numbered consecutively throughout the sessions (sessios 2 has occasion 16-32 for example). If day1 = "station", the numbers start at 1 in each session

I also realised that the occasions were divided by occasion length throughout the entire data period, regardless of the time period for each session. For example, say that the occasion length is specified to 10 days, but Session 1 spans from day 1 to day 98: From what I can see, when using the function spatialdetectionhistory, day 99 and day 100 would be included in the 10th occasion (along with days 91 to 98) and, consequently, the 10th occasion would be split between Session 1 and Session 2.

I need to think about this. If a record is in day 99 and your second session begins on day 99, it should be included in session 2. Records in day 99 and 100 should not be included in session1. When an occasion is split between 2 sessions, this should be reflected in the effort matrix. If you don't mind, can you test this please and report?



Please give it a try and also play around with the arguments (day1 = “station”).

I’d be happy to hear from you if it worked or if you encountered any problems.

Thank you!

Jürgen

Dear Jürgen,

 

Thank you very much for your answer and your codes. I tried this new approach and, I was able to create tables which can be used in the SECR package. However, as you can see in the Camera trap table that I sent to you, my data does contain multiple cameras AND multiple sessions for some stations (Station 22, as an example in my data). Therefore, when using the following code on the camera trap table,
camtraps_cam_stations_only_S <-camtraps_cam_S[!duplicated(camtraps_cam_S[,c("Station", "Sessioncol")]),]

, we only consider days for which the first camera from each station was in operation (camera 6 for Station 22, in my data), and not the following cameras (cameras 7 and 8 for Station 22). As an example, the Camera operation matrix contains only NAs for Station 22 from August 22nd to November 16th, even though Camera 8 was functioning during that period.

 

I looked at the effort (or usage) and, other than the issue raised above, it all seems correct. However, as mentioned in my previous email, I would like to consider the total number of cameras operating in each station (That is effort of 12 if there were 2 cameras working for 6 days).  

 

I thought of a quick way to work around these 2 issues (But unfortunately, as you will see later in my message, there is still a problem with the resulting table). If I run the following code:

 

camop_session0 <- cameraOperation(CTtable      = camtraps_cam_S,

stationCol   = "Station",

                                 setupCol     = "Setup_date",

                                 retrievalCol = "Retrieval_date",

                                 writecsv     = FALSE,

                                 dateFormat   = "%Y-%m-%d",

                                 allCamsOn    = FALSE,

                                 cameraCol    = "Sessioncol",

                                 byCamera    = TRUE,

camerasIndependent = FALSE,

                                 hasProblems  = TRUE

)

 

 

I get a Camera Operation Matrix which contains a line for each Station, Camera and Session. I then calculate the sum of cameras in operation by Station-Sessions specific groups for each day (Or I calculate the max (That is 1 or NA) to see if there is at least one camera operating on that day for a specific station). This results in a Matrix with one line per Station and Session, as we obtained with the code you sent in your last message, but also considering all cameras for stations with multiple cameras. Here is the code I have used (I am sorry if it is not very elegant, I am still in the process of learning R at the moment!):

 

 

is.data.frame(camop_session0)

typeof(camop_session0)

 

camop_session <- as.data.frame(camop_session0)

camop_session$Station = 'Station'

camop_session$Session = 'Session'

camop_session$Station = substr(rownames(camop_session),1,9)

camop_session$Session = substr(rownames(camop_session),12,12)

 

n = length(names(camop_session))-2

camop_session_sum <- aggregate(camop_session[, 1:n], by=list(camop_session$Station,camop_session$Session), sum)

camop_session_max <- aggregate(camop_session[, 1:n], by=list(camop_session$Station,camop_session$Session), max) #This can be used if I want to calculate the effort by considering only 1 or 0s for each station at each day

 

library(dplyr)

library(tidyr)

 

camop_session_sum <- tidyr::unite(camop_session_sum, "x", c("Group.1", "Group.2"), sep = "__")

rownames(camop_session_sum)<- camop_session_sum$x

camop_session_sum$x = gsub("\\__", "", camop_session_sum$x)

camop_session_sum$x = as.numeric(gsub("\\Station", "", camop_session_sum$x))

camop_session_sum <- camop_session_sum[order(camop_session_sum$x),]

camop_session_sum$x = NULL

 

is.data.frame(camop_session_sum)

typeof(camop_session_sum)

 

camop_session_sum2 <- data.matrix(camop_session_sum, rownames.force = TRUE)

 

is.data.frame(camop_session_sum2)

typeof(camop_session_sum2)

 

camop_session_sum2[, 1:6]

 

 

It seemed to have worked, but when I looked a bit more carefully at the resulting Camera Operation Matrix (that is camop_session0) that was obtained from the CameraOperation function, I realised the following: For Station 22, as long as there is 1 camera operating in a session, all other cameras in that session will also have a ‘1’ regardless if the camera was operating on that day or not (for example Camera 7 of Station 22 is not functioning after June 10th, but the matrix still indicates a 1 on each day following that date). There is therefore still a mistake and I am not sure how this could be fixed. I obtain the same result if I use the argument camerasIndependent = TRUE instead. Alternatively, I could separate my data into sessions and create spatial detection histories for each session.

 

I would be happy to receive any further thoughts you may have.

 

Again, thank you a lot for your help.

 

Best,


Vanessa
